title: Gatebraid N3 validator coverage report (gatebraid/coverage-report@2)
description: Successor to gatebraid/coverage-report@1, which is NOT edited and NOT retro-broken (@1 reports stay valid as @1). Introduced at M3 batch P-B1 (ADR-0037 decision 7) for two reasons the same batch created. (1) `target.schema_id` gains gatebraid/gate-run@3: the validator re-derives verdicts over the records Slice P2-S7 writes, and @1's closed enumeration could not name them. (2) IN-01, 'wrong pipeline exit code', freezes here -- the item ADR-0031's first reopening condition re-assigned from the N3-start freeze to corpus v2 at P's start because its assertion spanned two documents (this report and the target capture's invocation.shell_semantics). A verified property may now carry `exit_code_basis`, the validator's reading of the target's shell semantics, and the schema binds it: a basis that is uninterpretable cannot sit beside a passing verdict, and a shell basis without pipefail whose exit code is the pipeline's last element's is uninterpretable by definition. The cross-document half -- that the validator READ the capture's semantics correctly -- is the validator's own falsification at P2-S7. Everything else is @1 byte for byte in intent; the @1 text of every carried description stands.

report_id.description: Stable identifier, unique within its slice's evidence directory. Referenced by a gate record's checks[].output_ref and by a dual_platform_claim in a sibling report.

validator.description: Which committed instrument produced this report. Mirrors evidence-capture@1's `generator` deliberately: a verdict whose producer cannot be named cannot be re-run (ADR-0028 §4, 'committed, falsified, reused').

version.description: Frozen at delivery (M3-PLAN.md §2 N3's last Accept-when item).

source_sha256.description: IN-02 locus. A digest-shaped pattern refuses a `<sha>` placeholder; DETERMINACY-REPORT.md §3's positive control is exactly this class.

target.description: The ONE document this report re-derives verdicts for, pinned by content digest rather than by name. ADR-0028 §2: no row names HEAD, `git status`, or any state the act of recording it will move.

schema_id.description: The three interfaces frozen at N1 and the only documents N3 re-derives from (M3-PLAN.md §2 N1: N3 receives the frozen schemas and the corpus, nothing else). `gatebraid/gate-run@1` is deliberately absent: no new M3 record is written as @1 (ADR-0029 decision 2, P1-1), so a coverage report over an @1 record would be a report over history this validator is not delivered to re-derive. @2 delta (ADR-0037): gatebraid/gate-run@3 added; P2-S7's records are the first @3 records and the validator must be able to name them.

platform.description: BP-03 locus, half one. ONE report records ONE platform: this is an object, never an array, so a single run cannot present itself as covering both. A dual-platform claim is read from two reports via dual_platform_claim below, never asserted by one — the same rule evidence-capture@1's `platform` states for captures.

dual_platform_claim.description: BP-03 locus, half two. Optional, and the ONLY place a Windows-AND-WSL claim may be made. Absent means this report claims one platform, which is the honest default.

reports.description: Exactly two DISTINCT sibling reports. minItems kills 'one platform presented as covering both'; uniqueItems kills the same report cited twice — the cross-document claim BP-03 names, and `uniqueItems` is the one cross-entry relation JSON Schema does express.

recorded_at.description: THE PATTERN IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT; `format` is absent by the N1C/N1D measurement. Lexical RFC3339 form only — FIELD RANGES ARE UNCHECKED, so a month of 13 or 2026-02-31 matches. Range and calendar validity are the validator's own re-derivation duty, named here rather than left looking enforced. Trailing anchor is (?![\s\S]) rather than $ because Python's re matches $ before a final newline and ECMA-262, which JSON Schema specifies, does not.

trust_boundary.const: N3 independently re-derives record semantics from the captured evidence — it does not independently attest that the capture event occurred as described (that a command ran, in that cwd, with that unmodified output).
trust_boundary.description: `const`, not a free string, and structurally required. M3-PLAN.md §2 N3 states the boundary and requires it stated; a free field would let each report restate it, soften it, or omit it — the generator choosing part of its own contract, the class metrics@1's enum'd names exist to prevent. The em dash is U+2014.

sections.description: FULL-FILE COVERAGE (M3-PLAN.md §2 N3, the review-4 lesson). Every section of the target document appears here, each with a disposition. Discovery alone cannot detect what was never added, so completeness is asserted against this list rather than inferred from it.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the target document. The empty string is the whole document and is legal.

disposition.description: EXACTLY TWO, and `excluded` is deliberately absent — it is not an oversight, in the manner of metrics@1's missing `issue-closure`. M3-PLAN.md §2 N3 requires 'an explicit completeness report (no excluded section)'. `not_applicable` is a finding that must carry its reason below, never a silent skip.

reason.description: Required whenever disposition is not_applicable, enforced below. minLength 1 because the empty string satisfies `required` while saying nothing — the F7 correct-course class.

allOf.$comment: A not_applicable section that does not say why is the silent exclusion this format exists to refuse.

properties.description: Every verified property, each carrying exactly one of M3-PLAN.md §2 N3's four classes. A class may legitimately be empty — the plan says so — which is why no branch here requires any class to be present.

completeness.description: IN-05's locus: partial validator coverage claiming completeness.

unexamined.description: Pointers examined by nothing. Recorded rather than implied, so that `complete` has something to be false about.

complete.description: **`sections_examined + len(unexamined) == sections_total` IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN JSON SCHEMA** — it relates three sibling values and no keyword compares one instance value to another. It is recorded here as an explicit re-derivation duty of whatever checks this report, exactly as evidence-capture@1's `ended_at` names its own inexpressible relation, rather than left to look enforced. What IS enforced is the conditional below.

allOf.$comment: IN-05 KILL. A report claiming completeness while naming unexamined sections is the exact item: 'partial validator coverage claiming completeness'. maxItems: 0 is the expressible half and it fires on the mutation.

verdict.description: The re-derived verdict on the target document. Not the target's own claim about itself — that is the whole point of an independent validator.

findings.description: IN-03's locus: a checker never quotes what it forbids into a record (ADR-0028 §3). Findings are reported BY LOCUS AND POSITION, and `additionalProperties: false` on the entry below is what makes a value-bearing field — `value`, `quoted`, `text`, `offending` — structurally unrecordable rather than merely discouraged.

allOf.$comment: IN-02 KILL, locus one: 'placeholder survives its own check', generalized to its N3 shape — a check that failed to notice. A report cannot accept a document while carrying findings against it. Without this, `verdict: accepted` and a populated findings[] validate together, which is precisely a checker reporting a defect it then passed.

IN-02 KILL, locus two, at a DISTINCT schema path so the two mutations are separable under run-corpus.py's (keyword, path, schema_path, property, extra_count) locus. An accepted report whose own property rows carry a `fail` verdict is the same failure one level down.

A rejected report must say what it rejected on. The mirror of the branch above, and the ADR-0013/ADR-0019 class: an outcome must be recordable, so a rejection with an empty findings[] is a verdict with no locus.

verifiedProperty.description: One verified property of the target document. THE FOUR CLASSES ARE THE WHOLE POINT: M3-PLAN.md §2 N3 requires that 'a `replayable` claim is either replayed or reported `capture-trusted`, never silently credited', and the conditionals below are where that becomes a property of the document rather than a hope about the implementer.

locus.description: RFC 6901 pointer into the target. A locus, never a quoted value (ADR-0028 §3).

class.description: M3-PLAN.md §2 N3's four, verbatim and closed. `replayable` is deliberately NOT a member: it is the unlabelled credit the plan forbids, so it is not expressible here at all. structural: the shape validated against a frozen schema. semantic: a relation the schema cannot express, re-derived by this validator (ended_at >= started_at; a base64 payload's sha256 and byte_length). replayed: independently re-executed, and then `replay` below is required. capture-trusted: accepted on the generator's capture and LABELLED SO.

replay.description: Required if and only if class is `replayed`, both directions enforced below.

command.description: The exact command re-executed. A value nobody can recompute is decoration (ADR-0018 §2a; convergence-metrics-v2 §4).

pinned_commit.description: IN-04 KILL: 'moved HEAD / mutable ref recorded as replayable'. A FULL 40-hex object name, so the strings `HEAD`, `main`, `origin/main` and `@` cannot be written here at all — the pattern refuses them. ADR-0028 §2: mutable references are pinned to SHAs or excluded from the deterministic subset. Full width for the same reason gate-run@2 widened base_sha: an abbreviation unique today is ambiguous after the next thousand objects, which is a replayability claim the record cannot keep.

rederived_sha256.description: What the re-execution produced, as a digest rather than as text. BP-01's and BP-02's blocked remainders — sha256 over raw bytes failing to re-derive, byte_length mismatch caught — are recorded here by a validator that actually re-derived them; the ARITHMETIC is this validator's runtime duty, and what the schema enforces is that a `replayed` claim cannot be made without the re-derived digest beside it.

trusted_on.description: Required if and only if class is `capture-trusted`. `const` because there is exactly one thing such a property is trusted on — the generator's capture event, which M3-PLAN.md §2 N3's trust boundary says N3 does not independently attest. A free string would let a report invent a stronger-sounding basis.

interpretable.description: Whether the captured exit code says anything about the command the property credits. False when a shell ran a pipeline without pipefail and reported its last element's code (evidence-capture@1 invocation.shell_semantics).

exit_code_basis.description: @2 delta, IN-01's home: the validator's reading of the target capture's invocation.form and shell_semantics for the command this property's verdict rests on. Optional -- a structural property rests on no exit code -- but when present the conditionals below bind it.

allOf.$comment: A `replayed` class with no replay block is exactly the 'silently credited' claim M3-PLAN.md §2 N3 forbids: it asserts independent re-execution and shows nothing.

The opposite branch, absent which the constraint above is half a rule. A structural, semantic or capture-trusted row carrying a replay block is claiming re-execution under a class that does not mean it — the F6 shape, where `form: argv` was allowed to carry shell_semantics.
capture-trusted must be LABELLED SO — the plan's own words. The label is the field.

And its opposite: a replayed or structural row cannot also claim it was accepted on the capture. Both halves, because a one-directional conditional is the defect class F4 and F6 were written to close.

IN-01 KILL: a property credited `pass` on an exit code that proves nothing (IN2-02). The interim enforcement home named in fixtures/instruments/EXPECTATIONS.json known_limitation (N2's layer B) is now a corpus assertion.
IN-01, the definition half: a shell basis without pipefail whose exit code is the pipeline's last element's is uninterpretable, whatever the validator wrote (IN2-03).

finding.description: IN-03 KILL. There is NO field here able to carry the offending value, and `additionalProperties: false` is what enforces it: a report adding `value`, `quoted`, `text` or `offending` is rejected on additionalProperties rather than tolerated. ADR-0028 §3: a detector whose output lands in evidence reports findings by index and position, and its negative case uses a real instance with only its report sanitized. `extra_count` mirrors run-corpus.py's own R1 amendment — a multiplicity, never the offending names.

rule_id.description: Which rule fired, by identifier — not by restating the rule and not by showing what violated it.

position.description: Byte or item offset within the locus, where one applies.

extra_count.description: Multiplicity for a set-shaped finding (how many undeclared properties, not which). run-corpus.py added exactly this at N1D because one unexpected property and two produced the same locus AND the same schema path.
